The story does not have a balance between the two elements; instead, it relies almost entirely on 'scene'. Written in the format of a dramatic script, the story unfolds exclusively in real-time through dialogue and brief stage directions (character actions and interactions). There is no 'summary' to compress time and no direct 'exposition' to explain the characters' shared history or background. Instead, the reader must infer their past relationship entirely from the subtext of their real-time conversation.
